title: Fix fetch tool omitting table headers with <th> elements
author: Copilot
body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode#263128

The `fetch` tool fails to capture table headers when HTML uses `<th>` or `<thead>` elements. The accessibility tree represents these as `columnheader`, `rowheader`, and `gridcell` roles, but `processTableNode` only filtered for roles containing `'cell'`.

## Changes

- Added `isTableCell()` helper that matches `cell`, `gridcell`, `columnheader`, and `rowheader` roles
- Updated `processTableNode()` to use explicit role matching instead of substring matching
- Added test coverage for tables with `columnheader`, `rowheader`, `gridcell`, and mixed cell types

**Before:**
```typescript
const headerCells = rows[0].children.filter(cell => getNodeRole(cell.node).includes('cell'));
```

**After:**
```typescript
function isTableCell(role: string): boolean {
	// Match cell, gridcell, columnheader, rowheader roles
	return role === 'cell' || role === 'gridcell' || role === 'columnheader' || role === 'rowheader';
}

const headerCells = rows[0].children.filter(cell => isTableCell(getNodeRole(cell.node)));
```

The `gridcell` role was added to maintain backward compatibility with the original `.includes('cell')` behavior, which would have matched this role.

title: Fix LanguageModelDataPart JSDoc parameter names and class description

The JSDoc comments in `LanguageModelDataPart` referred to a `mimeType` parameter, but the actual parameter is `mime`. Additionally, the class description incorrectly stated it was only "returned from a LanguageModelChatResponse" when it's used in multiple contexts.

## Changes

- **JSDoc parameter corrections**: Updated `@param mimeType` to `@param mime` in `image()`, `json()`, and `text()` static methods
- **Class description**: Broadened to reflect usage in `LanguageModelChatResponse`, `LanguageModelChatMessage`, `LanguageModelToolResult`, and other language model interactions

```typescript
// Before
/**
 * @param mimeType The MIME type of the image.
 */
static image(data: Uint8Array, mime: string): LanguageModelDataPart;

// After
/**
 * @param mime The MIME type of the image.
 */

You can rephrase your prompt or continue in the panel chat. **After:** > Inline Chat is designed for single file code changes. This task is either too complex or requires a text response. You can rephrase your prompt or continue in panel chat. The fix watches for drops on the container/chat entry, recognizes terminal drags, and forwards them to the usual “move to end” logic, so behavior matches what we had before.

author: Copilot
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/274924 When running terminal commands in multiple chat editors, the chat terminal count button showed stale values until the terminal was resized. ## Changes Added `onDidChangeInstances` event listener to `TerminalTabbedView` to trigger count updates when terminal instances change visibility or location. ```typescript // Before: only listened to registration and disposal Event.any( this._terminalChatService.onDidRegisterTerminalInstanceWithToolSession, this._terminalService.onDidDisposeInstance ) // After: also listens to instance changes (visibility, movement, creation) Event.any( this._terminalChatService.onDidRegisterTerminalInstanceWithToolSession, this._terminalService.onDidDisposeInstance, this._terminalService.onDidChangeInstances // ← added ) ``` The existing listeners only caught explicit registration and disposal events. Chat terminals created in editors trigger instance changes that weren't being monitored, causing the count to become stale until layout forced a refresh.

body:
Fixes #issue_number

## Description

After window reload, `lastFocusedWidget` is undefined and the existing fallback to find a widget may also fail, causing "Attach To Chat" to silently do nothing.

Added fallback to automatically open chat view when no widget found, matching pattern in `terminal.chatAgentTools.contribution.ts`:

```typescript
let widget = this._chatWidgetService.lastFocusedWidget 
    ?? this._chatWidgetService.getWidgetsByLocations(ChatAgentLocation.Chat)
        ?.find(w => w.attachmentCapabilities.supportsTerminalAttachments);

// Open chat view if not found
if (!widget) {
    widget = await showChatView(this._viewsService, this._layoutService);
}

if (!widget) {
    return;
}
```

**Changes:**
- Added `IViewsService` and `IWorkbenchLayoutService` to `DecorationAddon` constructor
- Call `showChatView()` when widget unavailable
- Early return if chat cannot be opened

title: Fix terminal command attachment after reload for non-Copilot terminals
author: Copilot
body:
## Description

Fixes #issue (command.id undefined after reload preventing chat attachment)

After window reload, clicking "Attach to Chat" on terminal command decorations failed for manually-run commands because `command.id` was undefined. Only Copilot-initiated commands received IDs via `setNextCommandId`.

## Changes

- **`terminalInstance.ts`**: Generate UUID for manually-run commands when they start (via `onCommandStarted` listener). The ID is synchronized to both renderer and ptyHost using `setNextCommandId`, ensuring the same ID is used everywhere and persists across reloads.

IDs flow through existing infrastructure: command starts → ID generated in renderer → synced to ptyHost via `setNextCommandId` → command finishes → serialized with terminal state → restored on reload → available for chat attachment URI.

## How to Test

1. Open terminal, run any command
2. Click command decoration → "Attach to Chat"
3. Reload window (Cmd+R)
4. Click attachment in chat
5. Command should focus (previously would fail)

title: Fix text selection artifacts in expanded terminal tool output
author: Copilot
body:
## Fix for Unexpected Lines in Expanded Terminal Tool ### Problem When selecting text in the expanded terminal output within chat, unexpected gaps/lines appeared between selected text. This was caused by xterm.js's serialize addon applying inline styles with `height` and `line-height` properties to the HTML output. ### Root Cause - xterm.js's serialize addon generates HTML with inline styles on div and span elements - These inline styles include both `height: 18.2px` and `line-height: 18.2px` - These inline styles have higher CSS specificity than regular CSS rules - When selecting text across multiple divs with fixed heights, the browser shows gaps ### Solution Override both inline height and line-height properties: ```css .chat-terminal-output div, .chat-terminal-output span { height: auto !important; line-height: normal !important; } ``` This ensures proper text selection without unexpected gaps by: 1. Setting height to auto so divs don't have fixed heights 2. Normalizing line-height to match the font-size (12px) 3. Targeting both div and span elements that xterm generates ### Changes - Modified: `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatContentParts/media/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.css` - Updated CSS rule to override both height and line-height - Added span selector to cover all xterm-generated elements Follows up on #273175

title: Add chat session title to View Chat Terminals action
author: Copilot
body:
## Adding chat session title to "View Chat Terminals" action ✅

This PR addresses the issue of adding chat session titles to the "View Chat Terminals" action to help users differentiate terminals across different chat sessions.

### Implementation Status

- [x] Explore the codebase and understand the "View Chat Terminals" action structure
- [x] Identify how to retrieve chat session titles from terminal instances
- [x] Start the build process to validate changes
- [x] Add method to ITerminalChatService to expose the terminal-to-session-ID mapping
- [x] Update the ShowChatTerminalsAction to include session titles in the quick pick
- [x] Address code review feedback (optimize lookup, fix whitespace)
- [x] Fix undefined chatModel issue with fallback to persisted title
- [x] Fix chat session ID and tool session ID alignment issue
- [x] Fix memory leak in registerTerminalInstanceWithChatSession
- [x] Validate all changes with build and linting
- [x] Code review passed with no issues

### Changes Summary

**1. Terminal Chat Service Interface** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminal.ts`)
- Added `getToolSessionIdForInstance(instance: ITerminalInstance): string | undefined` method to retrieve the tool session ID
- Added `registerTerminalInstanceWithChatSession(chatSessionId: string, instance: ITerminalInstance): void` to register chat session association
- Added `getChatSessionIdForInstance(instance: ITerminalInstance): string | undefined` to retrieve the chat session ID

**2. Terminal Chat Service Implementation** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chat/browser/terminalChatService.ts`)
- Added `_toolSessionIdByTerminalInstance` reverse lookup map for O(1) performance
- Added `_chatSessionIdByTerminalInstance` map to store chat session ID associations
- Added `_chatSessionListenersByTerminalInstance` DisposableMap to track disposal listeners and prevent memory leaks
- Implemented all new methods with proper lifecycle management
- **Fixed memory leak**: `registerTerminalInstanceWithChatSession()` now checks if already registered and properly cleans up previous listeners

**3. Run In Terminal Tool** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/tools/runInTerminalTool.ts`)
- Updated `_initBackgroundTerminal` to register chat session ID alongside tool session ID
- Updated `_initForegroundTerminal` to register chat session ID for both new and cached terminals
- Updated `_restoreTerminalAssociations` to restore chat session ID mappings

**4. View Chat Terminals Action** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chat/browser/terminalChatActions.ts`)
- Changed to use `getChatSessionIdForInstance()` instead of `getToolSessionIdForInstance()`
- Now correctly retrieves chat session titles using the actual chat session ID
- Maintains fallback to persisted session title for inactive sessions

### Root Cause Analysis

The issue was that there are two distinct IDs in the system:
1. **Tool Session ID**: A UUID generated for each terminal tool invocation, used for linking the terminal to the chat UI component
2. **Chat Session ID**: The actual chat session identifier, needed to retrieve the chat session title

Previously, the code was trying to use the tool session ID to get the chat session title, which caused `chatModel` to be undefined because these IDs are not aligned.

### Solution

Added a separate mapping to track chat session IDs alongside tool session IDs. The tool session ID continues to be used for UI component linking, while the chat session ID is now properly stored and retrieved for displaying the session title.

### Memory Leak Fix

The initial implementation had a memory leak where multiple registrations of the same terminal instance would create duplicate disposal listeners. Fixed by:
- Using a `DisposableMap` to track listeners per terminal instance
- Checking if already registered with the same session ID and skipping re-registration
- Properly cleaning up previous listeners when re-registering with a different session ID

### User Experience

The "View Chat Terminals" quick pick now displays:
- **Label**: Terminal icon and title (e.g., `$(terminal) bash`)
- **Description**: Chat session title and/or status (e.g., `My Chat Session • Hidden` or `My Chat Session`)
- **Detail**: Last executed command (e.g., `Last: npm install`)

This enhancement makes it easy for users to identify which chat session a terminal belongs to, especially when working with multiple chat sessions that have created terminals.

### Technical Details

**Performance Optimization:**
- O(1) lookup for both tool session ID and chat session ID using reverse maps
- All maps kept synchronized with proper lifecycle management

**Robustness:**
- Proper separation of concerns between tool session IDs and chat session IDs
- Handles cases where chat session is no longer active by falling back to `getPersistedSessionTitle()`
- Automatic cleanup when terminal instances are disposed
- No memory leaks from duplicate listener registrations

**Code Quality:**
- ✅ Build: 0 compilation errors
- ✅ ESLint: No issues  
- ✅ Code Review: All feedback addressed
- ✅ VS Code Guidelines: Followed all coding standards
- ✅ Type Safety: Full TypeScript type checking maintained
- ✅ Minimal Changes: Only modified necessary files

title: Add configurable extension download timeout setting
author: Copilot
body:
Corporate proxies with security scanning can stall initial data transfer for 60+ seconds, causing extension installation failures with the hardcoded 10-second timeout.

## Changes

**Configuration** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts`)
- Added `extensions.requestTimeout` setting (default: 60000ms, min: 0)
- Scoped specifically to extension downloads from the Marketplace
- Registered in extensions contribution following VS Code patterns
- Tagged as using online services with APPLICATION scope

**Extension Gallery Service** (`src/vs/platform/extensionManagement/common/extensionGalleryService.ts`)
- Replaced hardcoded `REQUEST_TIME_OUT = 10_000` with `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 60000` constant
- Added `getRequestTimeout()` to read from `extensions.requestTimeout` configuration with fallback to default
- Updated 4 HTTP request sites: metadata fetch, asset downloads (primary/fallback), control manifest fetch

## Usage

```json
{
  "extensions.requestTimeout": 90000  // 90 seconds
}
```

Set to 0 to disable timeout.

Addresses @chrmarti's feedback to increase default before adding configurability and @sandy081's feedback to scope the setting to extensions only rather than making it a general HTTP setting.
